operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple lowercase ASCII (people, debate, debate_people); no spaces or mixed case, but columns like People_ID, Debate_ID, Num_of_Audience, If_Affirmative_Win are mixed case and must be double-quoted.
Tiny DB: people=10, debate=6, debate_people=5 rows; read_schema original_values is complete, no rowid sampling needed.
debate_people has a 3-column composite PK (Debate_ID, Affirmative, Negative); sample_fresh_primary_keys must dedupe on the full tuple, and composite-PK members get max_l0=30.

debate_people has two FKs to the SAME parent people (Affirmative, Negative) plus one to debate; fill_foreign_keys_consistently must handle multiple child columns drawing from the same parent column independently.
FK parent people.People_ID is a single-column PK (unique) and debate.Debate_ID likewise; no dangling or non-unique parents here.
No self-references, no cycles; table order is trivially people, debate -> debate_people.
debate.Date is declared TEXT and stores 'October 21, 2011' style strings -> dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date; TS will not parse these as dates.

debate_people.If_Affirmative_Win declared 'bool' but storage class is text with values 'T'/'F' -> Bool fuzzer emits True/False (Python bools), which sqlite stores as 1/0, contradicting the original 'T'/'F' text.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0; no NOT NULL/CHECK constraints, so no insert-time row rejection expected.
No unique single-column constraints beyond PKs; drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.
Party has only 4 distinct values, Venue 4, District 10 -> low-cardinality text columns where TS String fuzzer will produce many fresh random strings.
Age range 35-48, Num_of_Audience 90-342, People_ID 1-10, Debate_ID 1-6 -> small integer ranges; Number fuzzer full range is [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from INT args (none) so default scale.
operator_ts_expectations: People_ID/Debate_ID/Affirmative/Negative/Age/Num_of_Audience -> Number fuzzer (int family, no args -> scale default, is_int True); values perturbed by +-1/+-2 from pool or uniform in full range.
District/Name/Party/Venue/Date -> String fuzzer (TEXT/char family, length default 20); fresh strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char).
If_Affirmative_Win -> Bool fuzzer: w.p. p an element ('T'/'F' as strings), else True/False; mixed types in one column.

debate.Date stays String: TS will NOT generate 'October 21, 2011' style dates, so queries filtering on date format/ordering will see random strings -> likely FN (implausible values) and FP (missing real date ties).
Party/Venue low cardinality: TS fresh strings rarely equal 'Republican'/'Democratic'/'Doha , Qatar' -> queries with equality on these values get empty results -> FN risk.

debate_people FK columns draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; with tiny parents (10, 6) many duplicate (Debate_ID,Affirmative,Negative) tuples -> PK dedupe drops most rows, shrinking debate_people below requested size.
Composite PK dedupe on 3 columns over small domains (6*10*10) means debate_people effectively caps near 600 distinct tuples; requested sizes up to 2500 will be truncated.
Bool column storing True/False (1/0) vs original 'T'/'F': queries comparing If_Affirmative_Win = 'T' will miss -> FN; queries on = 1 may spuriously match -> FP.
Age/Num_of_Audience Number fuzzer full-range draws (up to 10^scale) produce implausible ages/audiences -> FN for range predicates like Age BETWEEN 35 AND 50.
No NOT NULL/CHECK so no insert failures; rows_ok should equal requested sizes minus PK/unique dedupe.
String fuzzer contaminate and fresh draws break joins on Name/District text equality -> FP/FN on text-join queries.
